Governance review

Stakeholders and interests

Board members, veto participants, ERIS signers, validators, contractors and voting accounts—in one review.

Attribution boundary. Public handles, roles and addresses are used only where the reviewed records support them. Address-level relationships do not establish exclusive custody, common ownership or intent.

Think Tank: six voters, effectively 4-of-6

A separate veto body—not merely an advisory group. Revoting is disabled and execution is members-only.

Across four substantive veto proposals, the five non-technical members supplied only two ballots out of 20 possible ballots, both abstentions. P5 contains no executable message; even four YES votes would not itself execute a Treasury veto.

The technical member’s abstentions are mitigating facts. Non-participation does not establish motive, and historical membership at every proposal height has not been reconstructed.

Validators, contracts and large holders

Validators are not one completed bloc

Galactic Punks, ERIS and Orbital Command voted YES. Smart Stake and Ceres voted VETO. HighStakes voted ABSTAIN. Eleven reviewed allocation-linked validators had no current ballot.

Only BackBone Labs and cosmosrescue among those unvoted validators had material current hub delegations.

Large balances need disclosure, not attribution by inference

The 215.228M-vAMP account remains unattributed. It holds Galactic Punks NFTs and received several direct Galactic Punks transfers, but their reward or payment classification is unresolved.

NFT holdings, transfers, timing and protocol usage do not establish common ownership.

Contributors and counterparties also belong in the review

Recurring core, comms, ambassador and moderator recipients; grant recipients; OTC counterparties; operations contracts; and the ERIS protocol fee account all affect the control environment. Contract and module accounts must not be mislabeled as people.
